newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: ARGENTINE BONDS END DOWN, EYE ON U.S. RELEASES.
newsitem.headline: ARGENTINE BONDS END DOWN, EYE ON U.S. RELEASES.

text.p: Argentine bonds finished mostly lower Tuesday, following U.S. Treasuries, as traders looked to direction from U.S. economic data due for release later in the week.
"We have to wait for Wednesday's figures and see what happens," said a trader at a foreign bank, referring to U.S. July retail sales and producer price figures due out Wednesday.
Traders said the market once again saw slow activity with a wait-and-see stance dominating.
Argentina's Par Brady bond fell 1/4 to 73-3/8. The dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 4 due 2002 was down $0.10 at 119.75.
"For the moment there is not an awful lot of action," said another trader.

The market paid little attention to the Economy Ministry's Letes treasury bill auction Tuesday, traders said. The government sold $250 million in 182-day bills at a cut-off yield of 5.70 percent and 250 million pesos of 91-day bills at 5.60 percent.
In the money market, 30-day peso BAIBOR, or the Buenos Aires interbank offered rate, fell to 7.1250 percent from 7.1875 percent.
